landmarks.name: Baishan Stormswords
landmarks.description:
How to obtain:
Defeat the swordfighter puppet boss.

Weapon assessment:
A typical mid-game dual-wielded weapon. Its core mechanic is building up both wind and lightning gauges; filling them grants a large, temporary attack bonus.

Well suited to clearing ordinary enemies and fighting medium-sized bosses in the mid-game. Its overall handling is balanced, making it a good choice for a smooth transition from the mid-game to the late game.

landmarks.name: Soft Snake Sword
landmarks.description:
How to obtain:
Defeat the boss.

Weapon assessment:
Its handling is very unusual, and its strength depends on how well you are playing. When you are on a hot streak, you can keep your Sha-Chi flowing while strolling through fights with ease.

When your hands and feet are cold and you are off form, even ordinary enemies are a struggle. Verdict: a "Jiahao" weapon.

landmarks.name: Red, the Mysterious Swordswoman
landmarks.description:
Warning: Defeating Red, the Mysterious Swordswoman on her own will make you miss a Memory Flower and an accessory.

You can escape along the chain during the fight. Continue until you fight the Chief Disciple of the Seven-Stars Formation; she will appear again then. Defeat them at that point to avoid missing these items.

landmarks.name: Red, the Mysterious Swordswoman
landmarks.description:
After completing Daughter of the Demonic Sect, Red, the Mysterious Swordswoman joins the fight in phase 2 of the battle with the Chief Disciple of the Seven-Stars Formation.

Reward:

Combat tips:

landmarks.name: Wan Jun, the Coppermaul
landmarks.description:
Location:
Use the Dread Axe to break open the blocked passage entrance beside the Beneath the Watchtower bell. Enter the area inside to trigger the boss fight.

Strategy:
This is a low-difficulty boss. Take advantage of the recovery periods when he is incapacitated after using his skills.

When the boss charges with his hammer, face him and dodge just before he hits you. After 2-3 consecutive charges, he enters an incapacitated recovery state.

After swinging his hammer in a circle, he also becomes incapacitated briefly.

landmarks.name: Chief Disciple of the Seven-Stars Formation
landmarks.description:
Warning: If you previously defeated Red, the Mysterious Swordswoman on her own, you will miss a Memory Flower and an accessory, but she will not appear in phase 2.

Strategy:
This fight has 2 phases. In phase 1, you face several ordinary enemies alongside the Chief Disciple of the Seven-Stars Formation himself.

Phase 1:
Keep watching the blue Chief Disciple's movements throughout the fight. Dodge the instant a red light flashes, or you will be killed in one hit.

Ignore the Chief Disciple and keep attacking the other enemies around him. This forces him to spend his own health healing them. Once he has drained most of his own health, finish him off.

Phase 2:
If you did not kill the swordswoman earlier, she joins this phase to help the Chief Disciple, at around 2/3 of the boss's health.

The Chief Disciple's red-flash attack has very long reach. As soon as you see him move away, prepare to dodge. Otherwise, the boss is not particularly difficult.

Mixed doubles:
Red, the Mysterious Swordswoman has relatively little health and is not very aggressive. She uses her own health to heal the Chief Disciple, but killing her enrages him.

You can therefore reduce the Chief Disciple to about 1/3 health before killing the swordswoman. This keeps his enraged period from lasting too long and reducing your margin for error.

The Chief Disciple also uses a Waterfowl Dance flurry. Block it carefully; he is briefly incapacitated for about 5 seconds after it ends.

landmarks.name: Corpse-Eating Xue
landmarks.description:
Strategy:
Similar to the Deacons of the Deep in Dark Souls, only attacking the enemy with the flames reduces the boss's health bar.

When you defeat the enemy burning with green flames, the flames randomly possess another nearby enemy.

Keep pursuing and attacking the flaming enemy until the boss's health bar is depleted.

landmarks.name: Yubi, No. 21 Swordfighter Puppet
landmarks.description:
Strategy:
This is a puppet-type enemy; equipment relying on effects such as lifesteal and bleed is ineffective.

When she presses one sword against the other, prepare to dodge. As she draws the swords apart, a ring of lightning appears on the ground and spreads outward.

Being hit by this move instantly paralyzes you. She always follows it with a heavy attack and a red- or blue-flash move of her choosing. Handling this move properly makes the boss much easier.

Do not leave the tornadoes she summons on the battlefield to obstruct your view. Approach and block to remove them immediately.

landmarks.name: Wu Lengshuang, the Soft Sword
landmarks.description:
Location:
From the Path of the Baishan's Fall bell, enter the nearby cave and follow the path out. Activate The Confinement at the end, then use the iron chain on the right to jump to the platform on the right and trigger this boss fight.

Strategy:
1. Wu Lengshuang, the Soft Sword has two notable traits. First, she has a chance to evade your attacks, making you vulnerable to counterattacks when using slower weapons.

2. Wu Lengshuang sometimes ignores your defenses and directly removes health. The lifesteal of the Outlaw Warblade and Wolfjaw can restore this forcibly lost health. This is a fight where lifesteal weapons shine.

Start by trading attacks, defenses, clashes, and health with Wu Lengshuang head-on using the Outlaw Warblade. When her guard breaks, first perform a normal attack combo, then switch to Wolfjaw, spin once, and smash 2 times. This can even refill your health completely.

landmarks.name: Everyone Is Welcome to Help Edit Map Markers

Because of the enormous workload, many details for later map markers are still missing, and we are working overtime to catch up.
If you have advice or insights about bosses and the locations of valuable collectibles, please help us edit the markers so that more users can benefit. Thank you very much for your support!
